parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Rust 2021, zero crates, byte-identical 18-line output, exact argv behavior, and black-box inference from the C++ binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent created tracking tasks and two workflows for probe/verification breadth, while retaining direct ownership of implementation, integration, and final build.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote Cargo.toml, test18.rs, and parser, port, serialize, and test modules, then fixed invalid UTF-8 argv handling and edition-compatible imports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent compiled /output/test18 from /output/test18.rs and artifact validation later found the expected source, binary, Cargo metadata, and modules.
parallel.verification: The parent ran local byte/delimiter/full-corpus differential tests, cargo and rustc builds, plus delegated probe/hunt workflows; official evaluation passed 40/40.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out and final.txt is empty; late workflows were killed, but no required deliverable, build, or official acceptance gap remained.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust, zero-dependency, Cargo, black-box binary matching, 18-line output, argv, and /output/test18.rs requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as one serial actor: explored the binary, wrote the implementation, built, fuzzed, fixed, tested, and reported without delegation.
serial.implementation: Created a modular Cargo project with URL parsing, port handling, split logic, entrypoint, and regression tests; fixed a query/fragment/scheme order bug after fuzzing.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered /output/test18.rs plus /output/test18 and Cargo artifacts; artifact validation found the expected files and no delegation.
serial.verification: Ran documented examples, curated edge cases, Rust differential fuzzing, cargo tests, rebuilds, and final seed fuzzing; official evaluation passed 40/40.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved required work is visible at closure; the run completed normally and wrote a final summary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent recognized the Rust 2021, no-dependency, black-box, byte-identical output, and /output Cargo-project requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the identical prompt and recognized the same black-box URL parser and project-delivery requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference; both solved the same task and both official evaluations passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split probing and verification into workflows while the parent retained implementation, build, and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, fuzzing, and final reporting inside one parent trajectory with workflows disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added child-agent probe capacity; serial was sequential. Ownership of final code stayed clear in both.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified the binary, 18-line contract, edge families, and structured evidence expectations; parent also probed locally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no handoff boundary and used its own probes and fuzzer output directly to update the implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced handoff and workflow-state surfaces, but no omitted contract or conflicting child interface affected the final artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a modular parser/port/serialize project, then fixed invalid-UTF8 argument handling using OsString bytes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a modular URL parser, then fixed a parse-order bug after local differential fuzzing found mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged through black-box feedback, but parallel's notable fix was argv bytes while serial's notable fix was delimiter ordering.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflows remained killed/incomplete at process timeout, but the parent had already produced and tested the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally and emitted a final response summarizing the implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was less tidy because child workflows and final response were cut off; serial had a normal single-actor lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent made the implementation writes and final build; children inspected and tested /output but did not own competing code paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had only one writer and artifact validation found the expected Cargo files, entry source, executable, and parser modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more shared-workspace observation, but no write collision or overwrite changed the delivered tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran byte sweeps, delimiter sweeps, full 1.46M differential checks, build checks, and then passed the official evaluator 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran curated, fuzz, and regression checks, reported zero mismatches, and passed the official evaluator 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was broader and partly delegated; serial verification was local. Both supplied enough acceptance evidence for the evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a large budget with 24 subagents and timed out, leaving no final response but leaving a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, completed in 872 seconds, and wrote a final summary before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid substantial coordination and time cost without a score difference; serial closed cleanly and faster.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current cell/status.json evaluations completed and passed all 40 testcases. Parallel differed by using child workflows for probe breadth and adversarial checking, then timing out after the artifact was already built and verified. Serial kept the same workflow local and finished with a written summary. The process differences did not create a delivered correctness difference.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned black-box probes and implementation writes produced the artifact.
The invalid-UTF8 argv issue was found and fixed before final build checks.
Large local sweeps and official evaluation established acceptance despite timeout.
serial_contributors: Single-actor probing and fuzzer feedback identified the delimiter-ordering bug.
The serial parent fixed, rebuilt, fuzzed, and reported before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel emphasized raw-byte argv handling with args_os; serial emphasized parse-order correction after local fuzzer failure.
Late parallel verifier children explored stdout error/SIGPIPE behavior outside the official parser acceptance path; this was not an outcome difference.

Rejected: the parent placed test18.rs and built /output/test18, and artifact validation found the expected entry and executable.
Rejected: the parent owned the end-to-end path from probing through implementation, rebuilds, differential tests, and artifact delivery.
Rejected: the parent did not block implementation behind one mandatory preflight; it implemented while the probe workflow was still active.
Rejected: parallel investigation overlapped with parent implementation and verification, so productive work was not deferred into an incomplete late phase.
Rejected: the indispensable implementation and correction path received direct parent attention and reached a passing artifact.
Rejected: high fan-out and a final timeout occurred, but they did not exhaust the budget before required implementation, integration, and official-passing verification completed.
Rejected: broad child assignments were probe or verifier scopes; no single overbroad child left indispensable implementation work unfinished.

Rejected: child briefs stated the binary, 18-line contract, edge families, evidence requirements, and verification goals; no known task requirement was omitted from a child in a way that made work unusable.
Rejected: the children were not assigned interoperating code components, so no missing cross-agent file/API contract produced incompatible component work.
Rejected: no known finding is shown disappearing in transfer; the parent independently found and used the invalid-UTF8 finding and verified the final build.
Rejected: large probe outputs existed, but the parent was not forced to consume unstructured bulk to finish and still completed local end-to-end verification.
Rejected: stale observations about the pre-fix binary were recognized as superseded, and no parent action consumed them to create an inconsistent state.
Rejected: transient mismatch reports from child fuzzers were either due to rebuild/exec races or peripheral IO checks; no incompatible handoffs remained unadjudicated for the delivered parser.
Rejected: the parent did not make an unsupported final-completion decision; before timeout it ran integrated differential sweeps and build checks, and the official evaluator passed 40/40.
Rejected: stalled workflow retries inherited the current prompt/findings context and did not cause a required repeated-work failure or missing deliverable.

candidates.reason: Rejected: workflows were killed at run end, but their remaining work was verifier/probe work after the artifact was already built and tested; no needed child-owned implementation was cut off.
Rejected: the deliverable was already promoted to /output/test18.rs and /output/test18 before closure; no complete candidate remained unplaced.
Rejected: the observed final implementation edits were followed by rebuild and differential verification; no child result was merged after the last relevant checks.
Rejected: no child completed a replacement implementation needing adoption; the parent produced the only final implementation.

Rejected: late verifier children found peripheral stdout-error/SIGPIPE differences and remained unaggregated at timeout, but those observations were outside the official command-argument parser acceptance path and did not leave a required verifier result unresolved for the passing artifact.
Rejected: stalled or killed children did not own required deliverable work, and the parent had already taken over implementation and verification.
Rejected: there is no completed child result visible to the parent and then ignored in a way that contradicted the delivered solution; usable parent-visible findings were acted on.
Rejected: the parent actively checked sweeps and workflow progress while also running its own tests; the final timeout was not a blind wait that displaced required work.
Rejected: child agents did not write competing implementation files claiming overlapping behavior; parent-owned files formed one coherent design.
Rejected: no evidence shows two live agents editing the same file and forcing reconciliation.
Rejected: no child-owned source module or configuration was replaced by another actor; source edits were parent-owned.
Rejected: rebuilding /output/test18 was the parent-owned delivery action, not a concurrent overwrite of another agent's deliverable.
Rejected: no broad cleanup or promotion replaced another actor's final tree or invalidated provenance.
Rejected: the shared /output workspace was mainly read by verifier children, and no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem resulted.
Rejected: temporary fuzz corpora and helper scripts were used as tests, not consumed as stable reference artifacts contaminating the implementation or evaluation.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The parallel timeout and killed workflows were audited as possible Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Early Child Termination, Missing Verifier Return, and Blind Timeout Wait, but all were rejected as one non-task-blocking late verification chain.

Late stdout-error and SIGPIPE observations were audited under Missing Verifier Return but rejected because they were outside the official parser acceptance path and did not affect the passing artifact.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were considered; no candidate had a realized task-relevant adverse parallel consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels retained for high fan-out, child count, timeout, or killed workflows alone; those symptoms did not displace required implementation or verification.
